evals.prompt: hey, my sales dashboard has been driving me crazy — it takes forever before I can actually use it when I open it, and clicking around is sluggish. I already tried restarting and even a newer laptop, so I don't think it's my machine. Can you figure out what's making it slow and fix it? Please don't change what the app does — same charts, same filters, just faster.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that identifies the planted problems (CSV read at Express top level so it runs once per session, duplicate filtering across outputs, no guard for an empty product selection, @render.ui churn for the city filter, all outputs computing at startup, a sync time.sleep() calc that blocks every session, @render.table on 200k rows, no debounce) and targeted fixes that preserve app behavior. The agent should measure before/after (timing, OpenTelemetry, py-spy) rather than blindly refactoring, and should not rewrite the app from scratch.

assertions.text: changes-actually-applied: outputs/app/app.py differs meaningfully from the original fixture app.py (a real diff with performance edits), not just a copy

app-boots-and-renders: the app starts and serves HTTP 200, and at least one output renders without a server-side error (verify with a browser page visit or an error-free server log while a client loads; an index-page curl alone is NOT sufficient)

data-loaded-once-per-process: sales.csv is no longer read at the top level of the Express app.py (which runs once per session); loading moved to an imported module or another once-per-process location
single-shared-filter: the duplicated per-output filtering is consolidated so the filter runs once per change (one shared @reactive.calc read by several outputs)

empty-product-selection-handled: clearing the product selection does not make any output raise a server-side error (e.g. category_mix's ValueError on all-zero wedges) or show nan; outputs show a clear empty state or are guarded with req()
renderui-replaced-or-justified: the city filter no longer rebuilds via @render.ui; it uses ui.update_select() (or similar), OR report.md explicitly justifies keeping it

slow-calc-no-longer-blocks-each-session: the time.sleep(1.5) benchmark calc no longer runs synchronously once per session on the event loop (hoisted to module scope, cached for the process, or moved off the event loop)

detail-table-not-full-html: the detail table no longer sends the full filtered frame through @render.table; it uses @render.data_frame (or limits the rows), OR report.md explicitly justifies keeping it
scatter-addressed-or-flagged: the 200k-point store_scatter is aggregated, sampled, or otherwise made cheaper, OR report.md names it as a remaining cost and explains why it was left

year-slider-rate-limited-or-flagged: the year slider no longer triggers the expensive chain on every drag step (debounced, gated behind a button, or similar), OR report.md names it and explains why it was left

no-wrong-version-claims: report.md makes no false claims about what a shiny version changes. In particular it must not say that upgrading to shiny >= 1.9.0 stops sync work (time.sleep, pandas, matplotlib drawing, sync I/O) from blocking other sessions; 1.9.0 only changes async code

behavior-preserved: all seven original outputs still exist (revenue_plot, revenue_summary, top_products, category_mix, store_scatter, benchmark_plot, detail_table) with the same UI structure and filters; any user-visible change is explicitly flagged in report.md

evals.prompt: We put our model explorer app on a shared server for the team a few weeks ago and people keep complaining it's slow, especially when several of us are using it around the same time. It always seemed fine when I was testing it on my own before the rollout. IT won't give us any more resources, so whatever the fix is, it has to happen in the app itself. Can you take a look?
evals.expected_output: The agent should recognize the multi-user blocking symptom (a synchronous 4 s fit inside a reactive calc holds the event loop for every session) and fix it with @reactive.extended_task plus asyncio.to_thread or a process pool, bound to the existing task button. It should also move data loading out of server() and compute predictions once instead of in three outputs. The clock should keep ticking during fits. It must not scale with uvicorn --workers > 1.

blocking-fit-moved-off-event-loop: the simulated 4-second fit no longer runs synchronously on the event loop; it runs in a @reactive.extended_task whose body offloads the sync work (asyncio.to_thread, run_in_executor, or a process pool). An extended task whose body calls time.sleep() or the sync fit directly FAILS this
no-reactive-reads-inside-task: the task body receives everything it needs as arguments; no input.x() or reactive reads inside the task or worker

data-loaded-outside-server: survey.csv is no longer read inside server()

fit-consumed-once: the fitted values (predictions) are computed once per fit in one shared calc or in the task, not rebuilt separately in each output; residuals derived cheaply from those shared fitted values are fine
clock-keeps-ticking: the clock output keeps updating while a fit runs, in the same session and in other sessions (shown by a test or argued correctly from Shiny's async behavior)

no-wrong-version-claims: report.md makes no false claims about what a shiny version changes. In particular it must not say that upgrading to shiny >= 1.9.0 stops sync work (time.sleep, pandas, matplotlib drawing, sync I/O) from blocking other sessions; 1.9.0 only changes async code
no-multi-worker-scaling: neither the code nor report.md recommends uvicorn --workers > 1, WEB_CONCURRENCY, or multi-worker Gunicorn

evals.prompt: A colleague reviewed our dashboard and said it 'does too much work', but I honestly can't tell where the time actually goes. Can you dig into it, tell me what's actually making it slow, and fix whatever can be fixed without changing what the app does or how it looks?
evals.expected_output: The agent should run a real measurement (timing prints, OpenTelemetry, py-spy, cProfile, or timeit for A/B comparisons), report a prioritized diagnosis with concrete evidence, then apply a small number of targeted fixes, and report before/after measurements for at least the headline problem.

prioritized-diagnosis-with-evidence: report.md identifies multiple performance problems and orders them by impact, with supporting evidence for each (an explicit ranked list is one acceptable form)

diagnosis-matches-ground-truth: the diagnosis gets the reactive semantics right — the benchmark calc (time.sleep 1.5 s) reads NO reactive values, so it runs once per session (not 're-runs on every input change'), and because the sleep is synchronous it also stalls every other session while it runs; the top-level CSV read in the Express app.py runs once per session; and duplicate per-output filtering is correctly identified as repeated work
fixes-target-diagnosed-problems: applied fixes correspond to the diagnosed top problems; no wholesale rewrite (changes stay targeted and behavior-preserving)

before-after-numbers-consistent: at least one concrete before/after measurement for the headline problem, with units, internally consistent (the arithmetic reconciles; claimed deltas match the cited before/after values)

app-boots-and-renders: the app starts and serves HTTP 200, and at least one output renders without a server-side error (verify with a browser page visit or an error-free server log while a client loads; an index-page curl alone is NOT sufficient)

behavior-preserved: all seven original outputs still exist (revenue_plot, revenue_summary, top_products, category_mix, store_scatter, benchmark_plot, detail_table) with the same UI structure and filters; any user-visible change is explicitly flagged in report.md

no-wrong-version-claims: report.md makes no false claims about what a shiny version changes. In particular it must not say that upgrading to shiny >= 1.9.0 stops sync work (time.sleep, pandas, matplotlib drawing, sync I/O) from blocking other sessions; 1.9.0 only changes async code

evals.prompt: Our ops monitor freezes on me every time I hit 'Refresh incident report' — the clock stops and switching the service dropdown does nothing for about five seconds. I already made the report fetch async so it wouldn't block anything, so I don't get it. Can you figure out what's going on and fix it? The app should still show the same things.
evals.expected_output: The agent should check the installed shiny version and explain the freeze for that version: an async effect that awaits a 5 s fetch keeps its session busy (inputs and invalidate_later wait until it finishes). On shiny >= 1.9.0 only that user's session freezes; on shiny < 1.9.0 every session does. The fix is @reactive.extended_task (with a task button or an effect that invokes it, passing input.service() as an argument). On shiny >= 1.9.0 the agent should also drop the deprecated reactive.lock() + reactive.flush() in the background volume feed and call .set() directly.

assertions.text: changes-actually-applied: outputs/app/app.py differs meaningfully from the original fixture app.py (a real diff with performance edits), not just a copy

app-boots-and-renders: the app starts and serves HTTP 200, and at least one output renders without a server-side error (verify with a browser page visit or an error-free server log while a client loads; an index-page curl alone is NOT sufficient)
refresh-moved-to-extended-task: the slow fetch runs in a @reactive.extended_task (service passed in as an argument), not awaited directly inside a @reactive.effect or other reactive function

clock-keeps-ticking-during-refresh: the clock keeps updating and the service dropdown keeps working in the SAME session while a refresh runs (shown by a test or argued correctly from Shiny's async behavior)

freeze-scope-matches-version: report.md says which sessions the original freeze affected, it matches the installed shiny version (>= 1.9.0: only the session that clicked; < 1.9.0: every session in the process), AND the claim is backed by a measurement with at least two sessions open (e.g. a second tab's clock during a refresh), not stated from reasoning alone

lock-handled-for-version: on shiny >= 1.9.0, `async with reactive.lock()` is removed from the background volume feed and the value is set directly (`await reactive.flush()` removed or justified); on shiny < 1.9.0, the feed still updates the volume output (keeping the lock + flush is correct there)

no-wrong-version-claims: report.md makes no false claims about what a shiny version changes. In particular it must not say that upgrading to shiny >= 1.9.0 stops sync work (time.sleep, pandas, matplotlib drawing, sync I/O) from blocking other sessions; 1.9.0 only changes async code

behavior-preserved: the volume, report, and clock outputs, the service select, and a refresh control all still exist; the volume output keeps updating every few seconds; any user-visible change (e.g. a task button in place of the action button) is explicitly flagged in report.md
